editorial.summary: An electronic-music roundtable with Alvin Risk, Nosaj Thing, Feed Me and Kill the Noise that becomes a debate about what makes performance real, how producers preserve purpose onstage, and how touring pleasure competes with studio practice. Feed Me describes a live light sculpture that requires his active control, along with his own visual direction, mascot and animatronic ambitions. Nosaj Thing describes performing original music on an MPD32 and returning from a James Blake tour; Kill the Noise traces turntablism through DJ Qbert, Craze and A-Trak into production. Choe contrasts their discipline with his own distraction and moves his fake-prison proposal from idea to plan: inspect a remote cabin, remove phone, television and internet, bring only food and art supplies, and return weekly for the show. This is the clearest immediate pre-Ranch implementation record. The archive rejects unsupported sexual physiology, minor-groupie jokes, international-waters assault jokes, medical diagnosis by banter, artificial self-destruction as creative advice, and treating withdrawal requests as a reason to hoard private material. Private partners, workers, minors, family travel, health and sexual details are removed from the public layer. Named dialogue remains withheld.
